source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed building fire-safety checks

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Record the date and time of the failed inspection.
3. List the specific fire safety standards that were not met (e.g., inoperable fire sprinklers, blocked fire exits, missing or expired fire extinguishers, etc.).
4. Detail the specific location(s) where the violations occurred within the building.
5. Include the names and titles of the inspector and the building owner or responsible party present at the time of inspection.
6. Describe any immediate hazards noted during the inspection (e.g., active fire hazards, obstructed pathways, etc.).
7. Note any corrective actions required by the fire safety authority and their respective deadlines.
8. Include photos or other visual documentation of the failed inspection findings (if available).
9. Summarize the overall compliance status of the building in relation to the fire safety code.
10. Attach any additional inspection documents, citations, notices, or warnings issued as a result of the failed checks.
11.
